metrics.|S21| between station planes: 0.981263 = -0.164 dB between x = 10.40 mm and x = 20.00 mm, 9.60 mm apart: one plane at each end, its forward wave taken from the algebra that splits v and i, and the two divided.  No fit stands between the planes -- a fit would average the field over the stations it was handed, and a load reads as a fraction of itself that way.  With a load in the mesh this is a ratio of ratios: the plane ratio above divided by the same plane ratio from an identical run with no load, and the line's own delay and impedance -- its beta and its zc -- are taken from that load-free twin, because this record's own fit spans the cut.  The line divides itself out either way (on a record that never carried a load the twin is the record itself), and what survives the division is the wave's own fate over this span, decay and all
metrics.G1 (|S21| within 1 % of unity): -1.874 % from unity, outside the 1 per cent a transmitting length is asked for.  The difference is real and not noise: with no ohmic loss in the solver, a decay this size is power leaving the guided mode for the surrounding matched layers, and the row below that exponentiates the fitted alpha states the same decay from a different measurement
metrics.passivity bound: |S11|^2 + |S21|^2 betwe: 0.962933 from |S11|^2 = 0.000056 plus |S21|^2 = 0.962876: a passive network must satisfy |S11|^2 + |S21|^2 <= 1, and the two sides of that bound are two different claims.  Above 1 is a bug.  Near 1 is what a model with no material loss should return, because the sum is the power budget of the two station planes and with nothing in the model to absorb energy there is nothing for it to be short of.  Well below 1 is power that left through something the two planes do not see -- an absorbing boundary close enough to the line, a source that radiates -- and that sink has to be found before any number from this run is quoted.  The plain sum is legitimate here because both magnitudes are read on the same cross-section, the two station planes, and the split hands both of them the one zc chosen for this record: the per-plane sqrt(Re zc) weighting is then the same factor on both terms and cancels, where two planes on different cross-sections would need it written out.

metrics.|S21| implied by the absorbed work: Charged to the station span (an upper bound): 0.957534 = -0.377 dB, 4.247 % below unity over the 9.60 mm between the first and last station plane. Basis: the work the matched layers removed during the 1800 settled (post-warm-up) steps, split by wall family -- 8.313 % of it at the lateral walls (ymin, ymax plus the top) and 91.687 % at the end walls (xmin, xmax), the box having no other exit because every remaining face is PEC. Normalisation: every joule is measured against the total removed work in that window, and in the steady state every joule injected is absorbed, so that total is the injected power and the lateral share is the share of the injected power lost sideways -- a statement about steady state only, which is why the warm-up steps are excluded from it. This is an accounting bound over the travelled length 9.60 mm, not a fitted exponential: the lateral walls run the whole box length and all their work is charged to this shorter span, so the loss it implies is if anything an over-estimate. Per unit length of line it is 1.6760 Np/m = 0.01456 dB/mm: the lateral walls removed 2.399667e-07 J in the same 1800 steps in which the run put 2.886668e-06 J into the box, and they run 24.80 mm of line, so the work per metre is 2 * alpha * P. Over the 9.60 mm of the station span that rate is exp(-alpha L) = 0.984039, 1.596 % below unity. That is the number to set a fitted alpha against; the 4.247 % above charges every metre of wall to a span 2.58 times shorter and so reads 2.66 times too large. In loss, not magnitude: the per-unit-length rate above puts 1.596 % below unity over the 9.60 mm, against 2.880 % from exp(-alpha L) above, so the fitted decay reads 1.80 times the rate the lateral walls actually removed (the two-wave alpha, 0.02554 dB/mm, 2.784 % over the same span, 1.74 times the leaked rate). The direct measurement sides with the accounting, not with the fit: the station-plane |S21| row is 1.874 % below unity, an effective 1.9703 Np/m = 0.01711 dB/mm, 14.8 % from the leaked rate. This row therefore believes the per-unit-length rate: of the three it is the only one that both counts joules and agrees with the amplitude ratio, whereas a decay 1.80 times faster would have to be paid for by lateral work this account does not see -- and it sees 8.313 % of the injected power, with the end walls taking the rest.
